name: OCaml
summary: Statically typed ML-family language from Inria with Hindley-Milner type inference, algebraic data types and pattern matching, a powerful module system (signatures, functors, first-class modules), a structural object system and, since OCaml 5, shared-memory parallelism (domains) and effect handlers. Compiles to bytecode and native code.

level_notes.0: The Inria distribution (ocaml/ocaml: ocamlc bytecode compiler, ocamlopt native compiler, C runtime) is the reference implementation and effectively the definition. js_of_ocaml, Melange and OxCaml reuse its front end; camlboot is an independent bootstrap interpreter.
level_notes.1: There is no standard or formal specification of full OCaml. Part II of 'The OCaml Manual' (the language reference, with BNF) is the authoritative prose description; language changes go through ocaml/RFCs and pull requests against the compiler. Formal semantics exist only for subsets (OCaml light) and for individual features (objects, modules, effects, the memory model).
level_notes.2: Part I of the official manual is a tutorial and is listed at level 2. Real World OCaml and the Cornell CS 3110 textbook are the main free books.
